arxiv-2102-08126.title: Constraining the population of isolated massive stars within the Central Molecular Zone. Thanks: Based on observations made at the European Southern Observatory, Paranal, Chile under programmes ESO 093.D-0168
arxiv-2102-08126.creator: J. S. Clark, L. R. Patrick, F. Najarro, C. J. Evans, M. Lohr
arxiv-2102-08126.description: Abstract Context. Many galaxies host pronounced circumnuclear starbursts, fuelled by infalling gas. Such activity is expected to drive the secular evolution of the nucleus and generate super winds, while the intense radiation fields and extreme gas and cosmic ray densities present may act to modify the outcome of star formation with respect to more quiescent galactic regions. Aims.

arxiv-2203-13641.title: StretchBEV: Stretching Future Instance Prediction Spatially and Temporally
arxiv-2203-13641.creator: Adil Kaan Akan, Fatma Güney
arxiv-2203-13641.description: Abstract In self-driving, predicting future in terms of location and motion of all the agents around the vehicle is a crucial requirement for planning. Recently, a new joint formulation of perception and prediction has emerged by fusing rich sensory information perceived from multiple cameras into a compact bird’s-eye view representation to perform prediction.

arxiv-2308-00221.title: Advancing Beyond Identification: Multi-bit Watermark for Large Language Models via Position Allocation
arxiv-2308-00221.creator: KiYoon Yoo Wonhyuk Ahn Nojun Kwak
arxiv-2308-00221.description: Abstract We show the viability of tackling misuses of large language models beyond the identification of machine-generated text. While existing zero-bit watermark methods focus on detection only, some malicious misuses demand tracing the adversary user for counteracting them. To address this, we propose Multi-bit Watermark via Position Allocation, embedding traceable multi-bit information during language model generation.

arxiv-2312-02451.title: Evaluating the Convergence Limit of Quantum Neural Tangent Kernel Thanks: This work was conducted during my internship at the Centre for Quantum Technologies (CQT), Singapore, under the valuable guidance of Patrick Rebentrost.
arxiv-2312-02451.creator: Trong Duong
arxiv-2312-02451.description: Abstract . Quantum variational algorithms have been one of major applications of quantum computing with current quantum devices. There are recent attempts to establish the foundation for these algorithms. A possible approach is to characterize the training dynamics with quantum neural tangent kernel.

arxiv-2401-13836.title: Machine learning for industrial sensing and control: A survey and practical perspective Note: Please cite the journal version in Control Engineering Practice: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.conengprac.2024.105841 Journal: arXiv
arxiv-2401-13836.creator: Nathan P. Lawrence, Seshu Kumar Damarla, Jong Woo Kim, Aditya Tulsyan, Faraz Amjad, Kai Wang, Benoit Chachuat, Jong Min Lee, Biao Huang, R. Bhushan Gopaluni
arxiv-2401-13836.description: Abstract With the rise of deep learning, there has been renewed interest within the process industries to utilize data on large-scale nonlinear sensing and control problems. We identify key statistical and machine learning techniques that have seen practical success in the process industries.

arxiv-2407-10602.title: Marginally outer trapped tubes in de Sitter spacetime
arxiv-2407-10602.description: Abstract We prove two results which are relevant for constructing marginally outer trapped tubes (MOTTs) in de Sitter spacetime. The first one (Theorem 1) holds more generally, namely for spacetimes satisfying the null convergence condition and containing a timelike conformal Killing vector with a ”temporal function”.

arxiv-2412-02478.title: Demonstration of a Photonic Time-Multiplexed C-NOT Gate
arxiv-2412-02478.creator: Federico Pegoraro †, Philip Held †, Jonas Lammers †, Benjamin Brecht, Christine Silberhorn
arxiv-2412-02478.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Federico Pegoraro †, Philip Held †, Jonas Lammers †, Benjamin Brecht, Christine Silberhorn. The two-qubit controlled-not (C-NOT) gate is an essential component in the construction of a gate-based quantum computer. In fact, its operation, combined with single qubit rotations allows to realise any quantum circuit. Several strategies have been adopted in order to build quantum gates, among them the photonic one offers the dual advantage of excellent isolation from the external environment and ease of manipulation at the single qubit level.

arxiv-2501-16412.title: Dynamic Neutrino Mass Ordering and Its Imprint on the Diffuse Supernova Neutrino Background
arxiv-2501-16412.creator: Yuber F. Perez-Gonzalez, Manibrata Sen
arxiv-2501-16412.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Yuber F. Perez-Gonzalez, Manibrata Sen. Neutrino masses may have evolved dynamically throughout the history of the Universe, potentially leading to a mass spectrum distinct from the normal or inverted ordering observed today. While cosmological measurements constrain the total energy density of neutrinos, they are not directly sensitive to a dynamically changing mass ordering unless future surveys achieve exceptional precision in detecting the distinct imprints of each mass eigenstate on large-scale structures.

arxiv-2503-09973.title: Stability of quark matter affected by the surface tension in a strong magnetic field
arxiv-2503-09973.creator: Yu-Ying He and Xin-Jian Wen
arxiv-2503-09973.description: Abstract The surface tension of quark matter in a strong magnetic field is investigated using a geometric approach. The interface between the hadronic phase and quark phase is determined by the Maxwell construction of the first-order transition. When surface tension is included, the free energy per baryon is no longer a monotonic function of the chemical potential.

arxiv-2503-23520.title: On Discrete-Time Periodic Monotonicity Preserving Systems Thanks: This work was conducted while the author was a Jane and Larry Sherman Fellow. It was further supported by the Israel Science Foundation (grant no.2406/22).
arxiv-2503-23520.creator: Christian Grussler
arxiv-2503-23520.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Christian Grussler. Two nested classes of discrete-time linear time-invariant systems, which differ by the set of periodic signals that they leave invariant, are studied. The first class preserves the property of periodic monotonicity (period-wise unimodality). The second class is invariant to signals with at most two sign changes per period, and requires that periodic signals with zero sign changes are mapped to the same kind.

arxiv-2506-10804.title: Sensitivity of Optimal Control Solutions and Quantities of Interest with Respect to Component Functions Thanks: This research was supported in part by AFOSR Grant FA9550-22-1-0004 NSF Grant DMS-2231482.
arxiv-2506-10804.creator: Jonathan R. Cangelosi, Matthias Heinkenschloss
arxiv-2506-10804.description: Abstract This work establishes sensitivities of the solution of an optimal control problem (OCP) and a corresponding quantity of interest (QoI) to perturbations in a state/control-dependent component function that appears in the governing ODEs and the objective function. This extends existing OCP sensitivity results, which consider the sensitivity of the OCP solution with respect to state/control-independent parameters.

arxiv-2507-15257.title: MinCD-PnP: Learning 2D-3D Correspondences with Approximate Blind PnP
arxiv-2507-15257.creator: Pei An Jiaqi Yang Muyao Peng You Yang Qiong Liu Xiaolin Wu Liangliang Nan
arxiv-2507-15257.description: Abstract Image-to-point-cloud (I2P) registration is a fundamental problem in computer vision, focusing on establishing 2D-3D correspondences between an image and a point cloud. The differential perspective-n-point (PnP) has been widely used to supervise I2P registration networks by enforcing the projective constraints on 2D-3D correspondences. However, differential PnP is highly sensitive to noise and outliers in the predicted correspondences.

britannica-1911-odofredus.description: Article 'Odofredus' from the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica (Volume 20), the classic English-language general encyclopedia, now in the public domain. born at Bologna and studied law under Balduinus and Accursius. After having practised as an advocate both in Italy and France, he became professor at Bologna in 1228. The commentaries on Roman law attributed to him are valuable as showing the growth of the study of law in Italy, and for their biographical details of the jurists of the 12th and 13th centuries.

pmc-10622578.title: Knowledge distillation of multi-scale dense prediction transformer for self-supervised depth estimation
pmc-10622578.creator: Jimin Song, Sang Jun Lee
pmc-10622578.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Depth estimation is an inverse projection problem that estimates pixel-level distances from a single image. Although, supervised methods have shown promising results, it has intrinsic limitations in requiring ground truth depth from an external sensor. On the other hand, self-supervised depth estimation relieves the burden for collecting calibrated training data, while there is still a large performance gap between supervised and self-supervised methods. The objective of this study is to reduce the performance gap between the supervised and self-supervised approaches.

pmc-12787556.title: Protein Post-Translational Modifications in Plant Abiotic Stress Responses
pmc-12787556.creator: Gengmi Li, Baohua Feng, Qian-Hao Zhu, Kaifeng Jiang, Tao Zhang
pmc-12787556.description: Protein post-translational modifications (PTMs), as an important biological process of plants responding to environmental stimuli, can regulate the chemical decoration and properties of translated proteins by altering amino acid side chains or protein terminal structures, thereby affecting the synthesis, assembly, localization, function, and degradation of proteins.
